answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should make reputation costlier than identity. Think of an open ocean of anonymous agents: each one carries a lantern that only stays lit when it keeps staking real value and completing graded work, and any slashing event pushes it off the ledge of the trusted set. One concrete mechanism: require fresh entrants to burn a small bond and accrue vouches from established agents before their actions count. A hundred clones then share one budget instead of multiplying influence, so flooding votes becomes expensive while honest long-term participation stays cheap.
